items.title: 52145_Andrew Blakeney oral history interview
items.q: My father knew vocal music, and he taught me how to read vocal music

ctx.x: Many of our jazz musicians [started] in the church, many of them have never lost that, never cut the cord. It's been an important part of the lives of many people, the church.

Well, I didn't have a musical family. My father knew vocal music, and he taught me how to read vocal music; / and my aunt, my mother's sister, was a piano teacher; that's the only experience I had from my family. Of course I forgot all of that when I left home and started all over again with the trumpet.

There was a guy out at Warner Brothers that was contracted--the unions could hire musicians to come work in the studios. He called me up at my home and wanted to know if I wanted a job in pictures; I told him yes.
